headline: Record volumes lift revenue, losses widen, outlook raised
summary_short: Natera's Q1 2026 revenue climbed 38.8% y/y to $696.6M on record test volumes (>1M processed, clinical oncology +55%), while the GAAP net loss widened to $85.1M (-$0.60/share) as R&D and SG&A outgrew gross profit; management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $2.74B-$2.82B from $2.62B-$2.70B.
summary_long: Revenue grew 38.8% y/y to $696.6M as processed test volume topped 1 million units for the first time (+19% y/y), led by clinical oncology (+55% y/y, a record sequential unit gain). Gross margin rose to 64.7% from 63.1% on stronger ASPs, despite ~2% of transient drag from Foresight-deal stock comp and volume-driven COGS. R&D ($210.7M, +$81.6M y/y) and SG&A ($327.9M, +$61.0M y/y) together outpaced the $134.1M gross-profit gain, widening the operating loss to $93.5M and net loss to $85.1M (-$0.60/share) from $66.9M (-$0.50/share). Cash and investments rose to $1,087.9M from $1,076.1M at year-end. Natera raised FY2026 guidance: revenue to $2.74B-$2.82B (from $2.62B-$2.70B), gross margin to 64%-66% (from 63%-65%), and R&D to $800M-$900M (from $750M-$850M); SG&A guidance held at $1.125B-$1.225B.

drivers.explanation: Company frames the quarter as a record — first time exceeding 1M processed tests, record sequential oncology unit growth — supporting a raised full-year revenue, margin and R&D outlook.
Growth driven by strong ASP trends across women's health, organ health and oncology, continued Signatera revenue ramp, and test volume up 19% y/y (oncology +55%).

Margin rose to 64.7% from 63.1% on ASP step-ups and efficient Signatera cost of goods, partly offset by ~2% transient drag from Foresight acquisition stock comp and volume-driven receive/report costs.
R&D (+$81.6M y/y) and SG&A (+$61.0M y/y) combined rose $142.6M y/y, outpacing the $134.1M y/y gross-profit gain, on accelerating clinical trials and commercial investment.
Net loss widened as the $142.6M y/y increase in R&D plus SG&A exceeded the $134.1M y/y gross-profit gain.
Cash and investments rose $11.8M q/q to $1,087.9M, per the release's balance-sheet summary.
